text:
incident-bot: P1 alert: region-fallback-loop detected for routing-policy=rp-7a3f. Multiple health-check flaps across us-east <-> us-west <-> eu causing repeated cross-region failovers. Paging oncall. 

ben (oncall): on it. seeing spike in error-rate for customer: enterprise-omega, latencies jump when requests bounce regions.

alice (sre): summary from probe-aggregator: 15m ago we saw health toggles every ~20-40s from us-east; routing engine treats as unhealthy and triggers fallback to us-west; us-west then reports probe failures and falls back to eu; loop continues until TTL expires.

carla (eng-runtime): hmm, that sounds like our fallback TTL + aggressive health threshold combined with policy match priority. I can pull routing decision traces.

carla (eng-runtime): attaching quick trace snippet (filtered):
```
[2026-03-15T14:21:34Z] req=0x7f2 route=rp-7a3f -> us-east, model_variant=gptj-fp16
[2026-03-15T14:21:56Z] healthcheck us-east FAILED (latency spike)
[2026-03-15T14:21:56Z] route fallback -> us-west, model_variant=gptj-quant
[2026-03-15T14:22:18Z] healthcheck us-west FAILED (kv-cache miss)
[2026-03-15T14:22:18Z] route fallback -> eu, model_variant=gptj-fp16
[2026-03-15T14:22:40Z] healthcheck eu OK
[2026-03-15T14:22:52Z] us-east recovers -> routing engine routes back -> repeat
```

alice (sre): notable: model_variant mismatches on fallback (fp16 vs quant) — that can cause longer cold-starts or higher memory pressure which might be aggravating the probes. Also see rapid TTL expiration: fallback TTL configured to 15s for this policy.

ben (oncall): customer-impact: 4.3% 5xx, 37% latency p95 increase for enterprise-omega. Support queue has 12 complaints.

dena (support): pinged enterprise-omega CSM. They reported degraded throughput and some request timeouts, no data loss. They want ETA.

frank (cust-success): told them we have a mitigation plan, will update in 30m.

evan (product): question — did anyone push a routing-policy change recently? rp-7a3f was updated last week to enable 'cross_region_preference: prefer-low-latency' and a new variant mapping.

carla (eng-runtime): yes, config change rolled 2026-03-08 02:12Z. The policy logic now tries best-available and falls back across regions quickly. Combined with health threshold drop to 2 consecutive failures it becomes oscillatory under noisy probes.

alice (sre): immediate mitigations we can apply now: 
- disable cross-region fallback for rp-7a3f (stop automatic failover)
- increase healthcheck grace from 2 -> 5 consecutive failures and bump fallback TTL to 120s
- pin model_variant on fallback to same family (avoid quant/fp mismatch)

carla (eng-runtime): I can push a targeted routing patch. propose commands:
```
# disable cross-region fallback on policy
redwoodctl routing update rp-7a3f --set cross_region_fallback=false --reason "mitigate flap"

# increase grace and TTL
redwoodctl routing update rp-7a3f --set health_grace=5 --set fallback_ttl=120

# force-model-family mapping
redwoodctl routing update rp-7a3f --set fallback_model_family=gptj-fp16
```

ben (oncall): please do the first one (disable cross-region fallback) then monitor. That should stop bouncing immediately.

carla (eng-runtime): executing now — applying in staging then can roll to policy quickly.

incident-bot: deploy started (deploy-bot): routing-update/rp-7a3f @carla.

carla (eng-runtime): applied to control-plane in 30s. Confirmed flag cross_region_fallback=false for rp-7a3f.

alice (sre): monitoring graph — health oscillation still shows on us-east but routing no longer fails over. latency for enterprise-omega p95 dropped ~20%. 5xx rate dropping.

dena (support): updating enterprise-omega: "We've disabled automatic cross-region failover for your traffic to avoid repeated region switching. We expect stability within 10-15 minutes. No data has been lost."

frank (cust-success): they ack. appreciate the fast turnaround.

carla (eng-runtime): next steps: schedule controlled rollout of health_grace and TTL changes. I want to roll that after we watch stability for 30m. Also we should reconcile model_variant mapping as a longer-term fix. Opening ENG-1256.

alice (sre): action items: 
- ben: remain on-call for 60m and watch escalation channels
- carla: open PR for policy migration script and follow-up monitoring alerts
- dena/frank: customer comms + collect example request IDs for deeper replay if needed

ben (oncall): ack. I'll also raise temporary alert silence for routing noise on rp-7a3f to avoid pager spam while we stabilize.

carla (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/432 — includes: pin fallback model family, bump defaults, add guardrails for small TTLs.

alice (sre): closing notes: root cause likely a combination of: noisy health probe thresholds + mixed model_variant semantics during fallback causing increased cold-starts -> further failing probes -> repeat. Mitigation: disable cross-region fallback (done), plan to raise thresholds + pin fallback variants.

incident-bot: incident P1 transitioned to "mitigated" at 2026-03-15T14:37:05Z; oncall: ben; follow-up owner: carla (eng-runtime).

ben (oncall): I'll hand off to carla in 30m after one full monitoring window. closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:

dena (support): customer updated. closing their alert after they confirm stable traffic.

frank (cust-success): thanks team. still capturing postmortem notes.

carla (eng-runtime): will run a canary for the grace/ttl changes next week and coordinate with product for rollout.

alice (sre): tagging retro: ENG-1256, SRE-438.

ben (oncall): end thread.
